submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad 'structure-delimiter' head: its resting state keeps attention on the text's first token and strength near 0.03 x max, and it jumps to 0.5-0.85 x max (scan peaks 0.87-1.00) at the delimiter that closes the second or later member of an enumeration - the comma, 'and'/'or', '][', or newline before the next numbered line after the second+ item of a series of three or more (digits, single letters, names, citation numbers, numbered lines, clauses), or the closing quote that ends an HTML attribute - where it attends the member just read with weight near 1.0; the same strong state appears at the second occurrence of a repeated element (a date, a name, a config key, a repeated method receiver). Predict INACTIVE for a bare pair of items in a phrase of four tokens or fewer with no other words ('bread and butter', 'gold, silver', 'tea or coffee', 'cats and dogs.', 'a, b.') and for a single-member form ('See [7] for details.'), and treat running prose of six or more tokens as borderline (0.2-0.55 x max, neither a reliable positive nor a reliable negative).

rival_explanations: Narrower: it is a previous-token copier that fires only when the delimiter directly follows a single-token member, so multi-token members ('He put on his coat, picked up the keys, and left.', measured 0.65 x max) and a closing HTML attribute quote after a long value stay inactive.

Broader: it is a generic content-attention head whose strength only tracks whether its attention lands on any later content word, so enumeration and repetition add nothing and plain prose with a salient noun ('The train was delayed because of heavy snow overnight.', 0.52 x max) fires as strongly as a run of items (0.65-0.85).

Different: it is a duplicate-token head that reacts only to a token repeated earlier in the window, so a fresh enumeration with no repeated item ('Sections A, B, C follow.', 0.83 x max) should be inactive while repeated prose with no delimiter should be its strongest case.
